breach.confirmMessage:
Matemasie can check whether your passwords appear in known data breaches, using the Pwned Passwords service of Have I Been Pwned (api.pwnedpasswords.com).

Your passwords never leave the device: for each one, only the first 5 characters of its SHA-1 hash are sent. The service answers with every hash that starts the same way, with padding added to hide the size of the answer, and the comparison is done on the device.

This is the only network call of its kind: apart from sync and the update check, Matemasie contacts no other service. The check runs each time the report is computed and can be turned off in Settings.

device.heading: Data kept on your device
device.key: The local encryption key is protected by the operating system (Windows data protection, Android Keystore). The backup files produced by the app are encrypted.
device.sensitive: Sensitive notes are additionally encrypted with a dedicated key, available only after they are unlocked (Matemasie passphrase, Windows Hello or biometrics). AFINOV SARL knows neither your passphrase nor your recovery key and cannot recover them.
device.storage: Your notes, their titles, tags, images, attachments and version histories, as well as the app settings, are saved only on your device, in an encrypted database (AES-256).

languages.heading: Languages and community catalog
languages.text: The community language catalog is turned off by default. If you turn it on in the settings, the app downloads the list of languages, then the files of the languages you choose to install, from a public MOSOBI repository (address can be changed). These downloads send none of your data, no identifier and no statistics. An imported or downloaded language only contains interface texts.

logs.heading: Technical logs
logs.text: The app keeps technical logs on your device to help diagnose a problem. They never contain the content, title or tags of your notes, nor your passwords or keys. They stay on the device, are sent to no one and are limited in size (the oldest are deleted automatically).

malware.appLock: The app lock is not a barrier against this kind of software.
malware.heading: Protection limit: malicious software on your account
malware.limit: Matemasie does not protect against malicious software running under your user account. Such software can read memory and the clipboard, record what you type on the keyboard and use the system protections tied to your account (on Windows, data protection, known as DPAPI). Your non-sensitive notes are therefore not safe from such software.
malware.sensitive: The content of your sensitive notes remains protected as long as they are locked and your password has not been captured. Their search information (displayed title, user name, site, last 4 digits of a card) does not, unless you choose to hide it.

network.heading: Network connections
network.intro: Matemasie only connects to the following destinations, and only in the cases stated. As with any connection, the server contacted sees the IP address of your device.
network.oneDrive: OneDrive (login.microsoftonline.com, graph.microsoft.com): if you set up sync or backups on OneDrive. Sent: the sign-in to your Microsoft account, then the encrypted files of your vault.
network.googleDrive: Google Drive (accounts.google.com, oauth2.googleapis.com, www.googleapis.com): if you set up sync or backups on Google Drive. Sent: the sign-in to your Google account, then the encrypted files of your vault.
network.webDav: WebDAV server whose address you enter: if you set up sync or backups on this server. Sent: your WebDAV credentials, then the encrypted files of your vault. The server certificate can be pinned to refuse any other server.
network.loopback: Loopback of the device (127.0.0.1 or localhost), on a port chosen each time: while signing in to OneDrive or Google Drive. Nothing goes out: Matemasie receives there the authorization code that your browser sends back to it.
network.breaches: Pwned Passwords, a Have I Been Pwned service (api.pwnedpasswords.com): only if you turn on the compromised password check, after your explicit consent. Sent: the first 5 characters of the SHA-1 hash of a password, never the password nor its full hash. The comparison happens on your device, and the service pads its responses so that their size reveals nothing.
network.languages: Community language catalog (raw.githubusercontent.com by default, address can be changed): only if you turn the catalog on, when its list is refreshed (when you turn it on, when you open the language settings or with the refresh button) and when you install a language, downloaded from the address given by the catalog. Sent: plain read requests, with none of your data.
network.lan: Local network: mDNS announcement (UDP 5353, multicast) and TLS-encrypted TCP channel (port 47652, or another free port) between your paired devices: only if local network sync is turned on or during a pairing, while the app is open. Sent: the service announcement, under a random name, with the address of the device on the local network, then the encrypted files of your vault, to your paired devices only.
network.stores: Google Play (on Android) and Microsoft Store (on Windows), through their own in-app purchase components: when you open the "Matemasie Plus" screen, buy, restore your purchases, and to check a subscription again (at startup and at least every 7 days). Sent: what the store asks for to show prices, process the purchase and find your purchases, under its own account and its own policy. None of your notes.
network.none: Matemasie makes no other connection. The note editor loads no remote resource.

purchases.heading: In-app purchases (Matemasie Plus)
purchases.plans: Matemasie comes in a Free plan and a Plus plan. Purchases (monthly or yearly subscription, lifetime purchase) go only through Google Play or the Microsoft Store: payment, your payment method and your account are handled by the store, under its own privacy policy. AFINOV SARL receives no information about your purchases from Matemasie; the store gives it the sales information it gives any publisher.
purchases.googleLibrary: The Google billing library built into Matemasie sends no logs or statistics from the app: its logging module is removed. Purchase-related exchanges go through the Google Play app on your device, under your Google account and Google's privacy policy.
purchases.receipt: So that your purchase turns Plus on for your other devices without a server, the device that made the purchase issues a signed Matemasie receipt (receipt number, product, price, date, order number when the store provides it) and records it in your vault, with the purchase proof signed by the store when it provides one: they are stored encrypted on your devices and, if you sync, in your own storage, end-to-end encrypted like your notes. Each device checks the signature of the receipt itself, and the store signature when there is one, with no other connection. The receipt is shown on the Matemasie Plus screen so you can match it with the payment receipt from the store. Technical logs contain no purchase information.
purchases.downgrade: Moving from Plus to Free deletes or locks none of your data.

remote.heading: Remote connections (RDP and SSH, on Windows)
remote.launch: Matemasie opens no RDP or SSH connection: it starts Windows Remote Desktop (mstsc) or the Windows ssh client, which connect by themselves to the server given in the item. No password is placed in their command line or in the logs.
remote.rdp: For RDP, Matemasie places the password of the item in the Windows Credential Manager, limited to your Windows session, for mstsc to read it: it is deleted as soon as the connection window opens, and at the latest 60 seconds after the launch. The .rdp file created on your device contains no password. A credential you saved yourself for this server is never replaced, and if Windows refuses this, nothing is written.
remote.ssh: For SSH, a password is copied to the clipboard, then cleared after the set delay (30 seconds by default).
remote.agent: The Matemasie SSH agent is turned off by default. If you turn it on, it only serves the keys you made available to the agent on this device, and only while the vault is unlocked. It answers on a local Windows channel reachable only by the Windows account that started it and closed to network access. Private keys do not leave Matemasie: ssh only asks it for a signature, and you can require your confirmation for each one.
remote.limit: These mechanisms are protected by your Windows account (see the protection limit above): malicious software running under this account can access the RDP credential during its short lifetime, and ask the agent for signatures while it is active and the vault is unlocked.

rights.heading: Your rights
rights.text: Matemasie sends no data to AFINOV SARL. If you buy Matemasie Plus, the store gives AFINOV SARL the sales information it gives any publisher (for example the product, date, country, amount and an order number); AFINOV SARL uses it only for its accounting, its legal obligations and handling your support requests. Otherwise, the publisher holds no personal data about you. You stay in control of your data: you can export your notes, delete the backups from your online storage and uninstall the app.

summary.heading: In short
summary.text: Matemasie works without an account and without a MOSOBI server. AFINOV SARL does not receive, collect or keep any of your data: not your notes, not usage statistics, not identifiers.

sync.encryption: It is encrypted on your device before being sent (end-to-end encryption): the storage provider only receives encrypted files and cannot read your notes. These services are provided by third parties, under their own terms; AFINOV SARL has no access to them.
sync.heading: Sync and backups
sync.lan: Local network sync, if you choose it, works through a direct, encrypted exchange between your paired devices, connected to the same local network (Wi-Fi or wired): no data leaves your local network and no online storage is used. Pairing uses a QR code or a one-time code shown on one of your devices.
sync.optional: Sync and backups to online storage are optional: they only work if you set them up. Data is then sent only to the storage you have chosen: your OneDrive, your Google Drive, a WebDAV server or a folder. If this folder is itself synced by other software, that software sends the files, still encrypted.
sync.signIn: Signing in to OneDrive or Google Drive happens in the system browser, directly with Microsoft or Google. The access token obtained stays on your device, protected by the system.

telemetry.heading: No telemetry, no advertising
telemetry.stores: The Microsoft Store and Google Play, which distribute the app, may process data related to its download under their own privacy policies.
telemetry.text: The app contains no audience measurement, no telemetry, no crash reporting and no advertising. It contacts no AFINOV SARL or MOSOBI server and makes no connection other than those described in "Network connections".

erasure.heading: Remote erasure and optional local erasure
erasure.remote: If you sync several devices, you can remove one of them from your vault and ask for its data to be erased; this option is not selected by default. The request is signed with the administration key of your vault and placed in your own storage: no data goes through AFINOV SARL. The removed device receives the request when it connects again and announces it for at least 72 hours, during which it can be cancelled with the passphrase this device knew or with the recovery key. It then makes a full encrypted backup kept on it, and erases its local data; its local backups are never erased remotely. A device kept offline never receives the request.
erasure.local: If you turn them on, the app lock can also erase the local data after a number of failed attempts that you choose, and the offline lease when the device goes too long without syncing. These options are off by default, on every platform, and erase nothing without a successful sync or a verified cloud backup less than 7 days old. In every case, only the data on the device concerned is erased: the remote vault and your other devices are not touched, and the files are overwritten then deleted (on an SSD or a phone, physical erasure is not guaranteed).

storage.heading: What your storage sees
storage.intro: Encryption hides what the files contain, not that they exist. The provider of the storage you chose (Microsoft, Google, the host of your WebDAV server) can see:
storage.layout: a folder named Matemasie and how it is organized;
storage.files: the number of files, their size and when they were written;
storage.devices: the number of your devices, each one writing to its own subfolder under a random ID;
storage.vaultFile: in the vault key file, the vault's random ID, those random device IDs and when each device was approved, each device removal (ID, date, whether a wipe was requested), the ID of the device that signed each approval and each removal, the generation number of the vault keys (it goes up when they change, for example when a device is removed), when your passphrase last changed, whether a recovery key exists, whether sensitive notes are set up and since when, how many times the vault settings changed and when they last did, and the key derivation parameters (never the passphrase or the key);
storage.cloudBackup: in the header of each cloud backup and in the file that describes it, its date, its type (automatic or manual), the version number of the database structure, the random ID of the installation that made it, the ID of the recovery key, the key derivation parameters, the size and checksum of each uploaded part, and a copy of the vault key file (never the passphrase, the key or the content of the backup);
storage.connection: the IP address of the device that connects, and the account the storage belongs to.
storage.hidden: It sees neither the text of your notes, nor their titles, nor their tags, nor the content of your vault.

purpose.heading: Purpose
purpose.text: Matemasie is a quick notes app that keeps your notes encrypted on your device and can, if you wish, sync and back them up, end-to-end encrypted, to a storage of your choice. These terms apply to any use of the app.

secrets.heading: Passphrase, recovery key and backups
secrets.text: Your sensitive notes and your synced vault are protected by your Matemasie passphrase, the same on all your devices, and by your recovery key. AFINOV SARL does not know these secrets and cannot recover them: without the passphrase or the recovery key, your sensitive notes and your synced vault can no longer be decrypted. Keep your recovery key in a safe place and make regular backups.

storage.heading: Third-party storage
storage.text: The storage services you choose (OneDrive, Google Drive, WebDAV or folder) are provided by third parties under their own terms. Their availability does not depend on AFINOV SARL.

sync.folderNotAbsolute: Enter the full path of the folder (e.g. D:\Matemasie).

action.deviceClockAhead: Check the date and time of your devices and correct the one that is ahead. The changes it has already sent keep their date, and those it sends afterwards wait behind them, even once its date is corrected: all of them will arrive here once the time catches up with that advance, at the latest after its length. No data is deleted.
action.localClockBehind: Correct the date and time of this device (automatic time setting, computer clock battery), then sync: changes from your other devices that are waiting will then arrive. Nothing is re-dated and no data is deleted.
action.persisting: Start a new sync. If the alert persists, do not delete anything: note this message. This happens after this device was restored, or if someone else changes the vault files.
action.vaultFormat: Update Matemasie on all your devices, then sync: another up-to-date device of the vault then gives the right file back to this one. Do not retire any device and do not stop sync until then. If all your devices are up to date and the alert persists, the file may have been changed.
action.vaultLan: Sync is suspended on this device; no local data is deleted and the passphrase is not at fault. Connect this device to the same network as another up-to-date device of the vault, then sync: that device gives it a valid file back. If the alert persists, a paired device may have sent a changed file: check the device list.

reason.deviceClockAhead: Another device's date is more than 24 hours ahead: its changes are waiting. Nothing is deleted; check the date and time of your devices.
reason.deviceLogUnreadable: A log file of another device is unreadable or has been modified: nothing more is read from that device. Nothing wrong is applied and no local data is deleted.
reason.deviceSequenceGap: A batch is missing from another device's log: reading that device is on hold. Nothing wrong is applied and no local data is deleted.
reason.localClockAhead: This device's timestamps were more than 24 hours past its time (date ahead then corrected, or date set back). What it had already sent keeps its date; what was not sent yet was re-dated before sending. Nothing is deleted. Check this device's date and time.
reason.localChangesHeld: What this device has already sent carries a date more than 24 hours ahead of its time: its date was ahead, then corrected. Until {date}, everything it sends waits on your other devices, including what you write on it now; what they send arrives here normally. Nothing is lost. This alert goes away by itself on that date.
reason.localChangesHeldNoDate: What this device has already sent carries a date more than 24 hours ahead of its time: its date was ahead, then corrected. Until its time catches up, what it sends waits on your other devices; what they send arrives here normally. Nothing is lost and nothing was modified in the vault. This alert goes away by itself when the wait ends.
reason.localClockBehind: This device's date is more than 24 hours behind your other devices. Its changes are sent to them as usual; theirs arrive too, except the most recent ones, which wait here until the date is corrected; none is lost. Check this device's date and time.
reason.ownLog: The log of this device in the vault no longer matches its history. Its new changes are not published and no local data is deleted.
reason.retiredDeviceFile: An unexpected file appeared in the folder of a device removed from the vault. It is ignored: nothing from it is applied, sync goes on and no local data is deleted. If it keeps coming back, a removed device may still have access to the storage: revoke that access at the provider.
reason.unreadableFile: A vault file is unreadable or was changed. Sync is suspended and no local data is deleted.
reason.vaultAltered: The vault.json file of the vault cannot be authenticated by this device. Sync is suspended and no local data is deleted.
reason.vaultFormat: The vault.json file of the vault is in a format too old for this version of Matemasie to read: it comes from a very old version, or it was changed. Sync is suspended and no local data is deleted.
reason.vaultRollback: The vault.json file of the vault is older than the one already seen here. Sync is suspended and no local data is deleted.
reason.vaultUnreadable: The vault.json file of the vault is unreadable and no copy is valid. Sync is suspended and no local data is deleted.

retire.pending: A device removal is not finished: it will be at the next successful sync. Check the connection to the storage.
retire.title: Remove the device "{device}"
retire.wipeLabel: Erase the data on the removed device
retire.wipeUnavailable: Erasure cannot be requested for "{device}": its version of Matemasie is older than 0.11.0, or is not known for lack of a recent sync. Such a version would erase everything as soon as it receives the order, with no delay and no backup. You can remove it without erasure. To request erasure, first update it and sync it, then remove it.
retire.wipeHelp: The removed device receives the order at its next connection and announces it for at least 72 hours before erasing itself, at a start of the app. During that delay, the person using it can cancel it by entering the passphrase this device knew: if the passphrase changes with the removal, or has changed since its last sync, the previous one cancels, and it is the one that opens the kept backup. Just before erasing, it makes a full encrypted backup kept on it; its local backups, including those in the folder chosen in its settings, are never erased. Erased: its notes, its keys and its storage access, and, on a phone, a Markdown export still kept by the app and the copies that sharing or opening a file leaves on it. The Markdown exports of a computer, and those already sent from a phone to another app, are not erased. A device that stays offline never receives the order. On an SSD or a phone, physical erasure of the files is not guaranteed.

Sync is stopped and nothing is erased yet, nor will be before {date}; erasure will then happen at a start of the app, right after a full encrypted backup kept on this device. remoteWipe.scheduled: Another device of the vault asked for this device to be erased. Nothing is erased yet, and nothing will be before {date}; after that, this alert will announce the erasure at the next start of the app, done right after a full encrypted backup kept on this device. You can cancel it with the passphrase this device knew before its removal.
remoteWipe.due: The erasure requested by another device of the vault is due: it will happen at the next start of the app, right after a full encrypted backup kept on this device. You can still cancel it with the passphrase.
remoteWipe.dueDeferred: The erasure requested by another device of the vault is due, but rejected attempts impose a delay before any new entry: the erasure is deferred. It will happen neither during this delay nor at the first start of the app after it ends, even if the app is closed or restarted in the meantime. Enter the passphrase after this delay to cancel it. Without a cancellation, it will happen at the start after that. Deferrals still possible for other delays: {count}.
remoteWipe.dueNotDeferred: The erasure requested by another device of the vault is due and the deferrals for a delay after rejected attempts are used up: it will happen at the next start of the app, even during the current delay, right after a full encrypted backup kept on this device. Keep the app open and enter the passphrase when the delay ends to cancel it.
remoteWipe.backupFailed: The erasure requested by another device of the vault did not happen: the backup to be made just before failed on {date}. Nothing was erased; it will be tried again at the next start. Check the free space and the backup folder, or cancel the erasure with the passphrase.
remoteWipe.cancelTitle: Cancel the erasure of this device
remoteWipe.cancelPrompt: Enter the Matemasie passphrase this device knew before its removal (or the recovery key). If the passphrase was changed on another device since its last sync, this device cannot check the new one: enter the previous one. The device stays removed from the vault, but its data is kept.
remoteWipe.wrongPassphrase: Wrong passphrase: the erasure stays scheduled. Only the passphrase this device knew before its removal is accepted, not a passphrase changed since on another device; the recovery key works too. The backup kept before the erasure opens with that same passphrase.
remoteWipe.retryAfter: You can try again in {delay}: a passphrase typed before then is not checked.
remoteWipe.throttled: Too many rejected attempts in a row: the passphrase you typed was not checked and the erasure stays scheduled. This is not a rejection of that passphrase: type it again in {delay}.
